result:
Solution 3 has the correct answer, $(\alpha,\beta)=(2,2)$, so $N(t)=\Theta(t^2\log^2 t)$. Solutions 1 and 2 both claim $\Theta(t^2\log t)$, which the lower bound below rules out.

**Why $N(t)\gtrsim t^2\log^2 t$.** Take $\bar P=(1-c)\delta_0+c\,|x|^{-3}\mathbf 1_{1\le|x|\le M}\,dx$ (symmetrized), with $c\asymp 1/\log M$ so that $\mathbb E_{\bar P}X^2=1$. Set $P_\pm=\bar P\pm\varepsilon\,x\,\bar P$ with $M\asymp 1/\varepsilon$. Then $P_\pm$ are probability measures, have variance 1, and have means $\pm\varepsilon$. For any query set $A$, the per-bit $\chi^2$ is about $\varepsilon^2\,(\int_A|x|\,d\bar P)^2/\bar P(A)$. On dyadic scales $2^k$ with $K\asymp\log M$ levels, the variance constraint forces the sup over $A$ to be $\asymp 1/K$. So each bit has $\chi^2\lesssim\varepsilon^2/\log(1/\varepsilon)$.

Bretagnolle–Huber then gives $n\gtrsim \log(1/\delta)\,\log(1/\varepsilon)/\varepsilon^2$. With $\varepsilon=\delta=1/t$, this is $\Omega(t^2\log^2 t)$. Solutions 1 and 2 miss this heavy-tail effect. Solution 2's construction is also inconsistent: its atom at $3/t$ with mass $9/t^2$ has variance $81/t^4$, not 1.

**Upper bound.** Coarse localization to an $O(1)$ window costs $O(t^2)$ samples, which is dominated. For the fine stage, random thresholds with density $\propto 1/(\tau\log t)$ on $[1,t]$ give a one-bit unbiased estimator whose per-sample variance is $O(\log t)$. Median-of-means over $O(\log t)$ blocks then uses $O(t^2\log^2 t)$ samples.

So $\log N(t)=2\log t+2\log\log t+O(1)$, giving $(\alpha,\beta)=(2,2)$.

CHOICE: 3
